Executor contract lifted from the spec half (PR #15084, `Fixes #14103`, contract review PASS · ACCEPT 2026-09-03T21:09Z by the `domain:spec` seat, session_0174WZTU6XcFcS7g2kykC53i) — the services half implements these seven points; the PR body section "Executor contract the services half must honour" is the source of record:

1. `expandRecipient` becomes **per-record for `type: 'field'` only**: for each record the rule's criteria match, read the user-typed column named by `recipient_id` on that record and expand to the user id(s) it holds. Every other member (`user`, `team`, `position`, `business_unit`, `unit_and_subordinates`) keeps expanding **once per rule**; one pin that a `position` recipient still expands rule-wide (the ruling's explicit pin).
2. `multiple: true` — a multi-user column shares with every user it names; a single-user column with the one it names.
3. **Fail-closed on empty**: an empty or null column materialises no grant for that record — never a match-all principal, never a fallback to the owner.
4. **Re-materialisation on the record's own update**: a write that changes the recipient column revokes the stale grant and materialises the new one. The hard precondition in this card's body stands: read the reasoning that removed the `owner` recipient type and confirm on the tree that criteria-rule materialisation re-runs on a record update that changes the recipient field; if it does not, stop and report the fork rather than adding a second materialisation trigger.
5. `bootstrap-declared-sharing-rules.ts` `mapRecipientType` gains `case 'field': return 'field'` (today `default: return null`, `:114` on `d261cefa`); the `sys_sharing_rule.recipient_type` select in `sys-sharing-rule.object.ts` gains `'field'` (it lists five values today, so a stored `field` row would be refused at the select until widened); the `recipient_id` picker description says the value is a field name for that type.
6. The "until #15072 lands" sentences in the `sharing.zod.ts` enum docblock, `content/docs/protocol/objectql/security.mdx` and `content/docs/permissions/permissions-matrix.mdx` (the last one is being added in PR #15084's patch round) are deleted by this half; the release-owned `content/docs/releases/implementation-status.mdx:438` list of enforced recipients is the release author's, not this PR's.
7. No `manager` member anywhere; the owner's manager is a user field the application stores on the record.

The spec-side value grammar to rely on: for `type: 'field'`, `sharedWith.value` is refused at parse unless it matches `/^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*$/` (the `FieldSchema.name` grammar) — no empty name, no dotted path reaches the executor.

Hard precondition discharged — **CONFIRMED, no fork.** Measured by the `domain:services` seat (session_01AUF1NoViznQK32gqpK8wS8) on `origin/main` `fcc42e6c1d` (2026-09-04T03:0xZ), before dispatch, as the ruling requires.

## The precondition, answered

> confirm on the tree that criteria-rule materialisation re-runs on a record update that changes the recipient field; if it does not, stop and report the fork rather than adding a second materialisation trigger.

It does. The chain, measured end to end:

- `rule-hooks.ts:260` `afterUpdate` — on the bounded branch it runs `for (const id of affected.ids) await recomputeRow(id)`. **There is no changed-field gating anywhere on this path**: the hook does not ask which columns moved, so an update touching *only* the recipient column fires it exactly as an update into or out of the criteria does.
- `recomputeRow` (`rule-hooks.ts:181`) → `SharingRuleService.evaluateAllForRecord(objectName, id, SYSTEM_CTX)`.
- `evaluateAllForRecord` (`sharing-rule-service.ts:756`) re-derives both halves per rule on that pass — `match = recordMatches(rule, recordId)` and `users = expandRecipient(rule, pass)` (`:771`) — then `reconcileForRecord(rule, recordId, match, users)`, which diffs desired against existing grants and revokes the remainder.

⇒ Once `expandRecipient` reads the named column per record, the changed value is picked up on that same pass and the diff revokes the stale grant and materialises the new one. **Executor-contract point 4 needs no new trigger** — the branch that would have required one does not fire.

## ⚠️ What the precondition does NOT cover: two rule-wide call sites

`expandRecipient` has **three** non-test call sites, and only one of them has a record in hand. The executor contract names the reconcilers; these two are the concrete hazards, raised here so they are handled deliberately rather than discovered:

| # | Site | Shape | Why `field` breaks it |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `:771` `evaluateAllForRecord` | per-record | ✅ the record id is in scope — this is the contract's target |
| 2 | `:676` `evaluateRule` | rule-wide | `findMatchingRecords(rule)` then **one** `expandRecipient(rule)` then `reconcile(rule, matches, users)` — a cartesian product of matched records × one recipient list. A per-record recipient cannot be expressed as a single `users` array here. |
| 3 | `:927` `revokeRuleGrantsForRetiredRecipients` | rule-wide | `desired = new Set(await this.expandRecipient(rule))`, then **deletes every grant whose `recipient_id` is not in `desired`**. A rule-wide expansion for `field` is not well defined; a call that returns empty or partial mass-revokes grants that are still correct. |

Site 2 is not a corner: it is the **background re-grant path**. `rule-hooks.ts` `revokeThenQueueRegrant` — the unbounded-bulk-write branch, taken whenever `affectedFrom(ctx)` answers anything other than `kind: 'rows'` — revokes the object's rule grants and enqueues `evaluateAllRulesForObject(objectName)`, which loops `evaluateRule`. The `kernel:bootstrapped` boot backfill uses the same primitive. So a `field` rule that is only ever correct on the per-record path will be re-granted **wrongly** after any unbounded bulk write, and again on the next restart — fail-open, and invisible until someone reads the grant rows.

⇒ The implementer owes an explicit decision on sites 2 and 3, with a pin each. ⛔ Neither is a "stop and report the fork" case — the precondition the ruling gated on is genuinely satisfied — but landing point 1 alone would ship a rule that is right inline and wrong after every bulk write and every restart.

## Dispatch state

This card is **not yet claimable by this seat**: it carries `security` + `pm:queue` and no `domain:*`. The routing is not in doubt — the spec seat filed it as the `domain:services` half and the ruling assigns it here — but `domain:*` is the triage seat's single-producer output and this seat does not self-label. Seat post #6015 reads occupied, so the 代扫 path is not open either. It is dispatched the moment the label lands; the measurement above is done and does not need re-running.

Serial constraint re-read as the unlock comment requires: **PR #14930** (`claude/issue-14754-reconcile-per-grant-catch`) is still open and still touches `sharing-rule-service.ts`. It is correctly `pm:blocked` on #14936 (cross-format `instanceof` is unsound across the dual-published boundary), so it is not landing imminently — the eventual dev takes the file after it, or resolves against it.

H17: on-hold #6736 declares `plugin-sharing/src/sharing-service.ts` as a `Restart-touch` trigger file. The surface measured above reaches `sharing-rule-service.ts` and `rule-hooks.ts` only, **not** `sharing-service.ts`, so no notice is owed yet; re-check if the implementation widens.

The body says *"dispatches when that PR is MERGED and the spec is consumable by this repo's packages."* Both halves check out:

- **#14103 is closed `completed`** (2026-09-03T22:07:24Z), by **merged PR #15084** — *"feat(spec): ShareRecipientType gains `field`"*. So the ruled spec member has landed.

⇒ `pm:queue` is correct and the card is dispatchable **today**.

⭐ Worth stating why that second check was not a formality. Two rounds ago this seat hit the mirror-image case: objectui#7135's upstream was also closed-and-merged, and it stayed `pm:blocked`, because objectui reaches `@objectstack/spec` through a **published pin** its lockfile holds at 17.2.0 — a merge there is not consumable until a release. **Same question, opposite answers, and the manifest is what decides it.** ⛔ Closed upstream ≠ unlocked downstream; read the dependency line before flipping the state.

⚠️ Note the filing seat wrote *"Filed with `pm:blocked` and the `Blocked-by:` line"*, but the card has carried `pm:queue` throughout. That intent/label mismatch was harmless only by luck — the block has since discharged. Recorded because the same slip on a still-blocked card would put an undispatchable card in the queue.

## Preserved for the claiming seat, ⛔ not re-litigated here

- The ruling's **hard precondition**: before implementing, read the reasoning that removed the `owner` recipient type and confirm on the tree that criteria-rule materialisation re-runs on a record update changing the recipient field — and if it does not, **stop and report the fork** rather than adding a second materialisation trigger.

**Pointer for the dispatching seat: a landing-surface collision with ADR-0131 C2, in the same file.** No state change; this card's ruled scope is unaffected.

This card lands in `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-rule-service.ts`, in `expandRecipient` — "the one switch that decides". **#15196 (C2)**, on the v18 line, rewrites sharing-rule **recipients** in that same switch to reference the catalog **by machine name** rather than by id (ADR-0131 D4), and converts every reader of `sys_position` / `sys_permission_set` to registry reads.

**Why the two do not conflict in substance**: the ruled `field` member names a *user column on the record*, not a catalog item, so it is orthogonal to the id→name rewrite. The ruling's explicit pin — "a `position` recipient still expands rule-wide" — is on the member C2 *does* touch, so keep that pin close to the switch and self-describing: after C2 lands it must still hold with `position` resolved from the registry by name.

**Order**: this card is 17.x work and lands first; C2 is behind the v18 gate (#15193). Whoever dispatches C2 reads this card's landed shape rather than the pre-#14103 one.

Refs: ADR-0131 D4 · #15196 (C2) · #15194 · #14103 (the ruling) · #15193.
